knowledge_point.title: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-5y &=-32 \\ 2x-10y &=-96.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -5 & -32 \\ 2 & -10 & -96\end{array}\right]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -5 & -32 \\ 2 & -10 & -96\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & \sim\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -5 & -32 \\ 0 & 0 & -32\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-5y &=-32 \\ 0x+0y &=-32.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=-32$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=-32,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

knowledge_point.title: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-5y &=0 \\ 2x-10y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -5 & 0 \\ 2 & -10 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -5 & 0 \\ 2 & -10 & 0\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & \sim\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-5y &=0 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-5y=0.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=5y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=5y \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}5y \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
